description: We are a passionate team of first-time space hackers, creative thinkers, and game enthusiasts driven by curiosity about the universe. Combining Unity development, AI tools, and NASA open data, we aim to bridge aerospace engineering with engaging gameplay. Though this is our first hackathon, our goal is to turn real-world space mission trade-offs into an interactive, educational, and fun experience for future explorers.
summary:
Beyond The Dust is an interactive 2D Mars mission design and survival simulation inspired by NASA’s Curiosity rover. Built for the Space Mission Design Game challenge, the game turns abstract space-engineering trade-offs—power management, wheel durability, scientific yield, and budget constraints—into hands-on tactical decisions.
Players pilot Curiosity from Gale Crater through Arkose Ridge and Bagnold Dunes toward Mount Sharp across 10 historical science waypoints. At each site, players view real NASA Curiosity imagery, choose between high-risk/high-reward or conservative engineering protocols, and read actual JPL mission archives. Featuring 5 custom scientific mini-games, a Ground-Penetrating Radar (GPR) excavation system, Habitat Dome shelters, and a JPL Lab upgrade economy, Beyond The Dust makes real Mars mission engineering accessible and engaging for students and space enthusiast.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

Beyond The Dust puts players in the seat of a Mars Flight Director commanding NASA’s Curiosity rover across three real Martian sectors: Gale Crater Basin, Arkose Ridge, and Bagnold Dunes. Players manage RTG nuclear battery power across Sol (day/night) cycles and dust storms while balancing wheel health over sharp rocks and energy-draining dunes. Using [R] Ground-Penetrating Radar to excavate subsurface science minerals and alloys, [E] Habitat Domes to survive Martian nights, and [M] for a live bird’s-eye tactical map, players navigate 10 historical science waypoints.

At each waypoint, players inspect real NASA Curiosity photographs and choose between two engineering protocols (e.g., running the 900°C SAM furnace during a -90°C night vs. conservative pre-screening), followed by authentic NASA/JPL historical archive logs. High-risk actions and Martian anomalies trigger 5 distinct mini-games simulating real rover subsystems:

1. Rock Core Drilling

2. ChemCam Laser Spectroscopy

3. Sand Dune Slalom

4. JPL Uplink Cipher Decoder

5. 3-Axis Gyroscope Lock (inspired by the Sol 200 memory anomaly)

Tools & Tech Stack:

Developed from scratch in Unity 6 (6000.0.73f1 LTS) using C#, custom pixel-art assets, procedural audio synthesis, and a 13-step interactive 60-second Flight Training tutorial.

Intended Impact & Engineering Trade-offs:

Students rarely get to experience real mission constraints firsthand. Through the [TAB] JPL Lab, players must decide whether to spend limited Science and Alloy budgets on survival upgrades (Titanium Wheels, Thermal Shielding, RTG Auto-Charge) or save Science points to unlock new sectors—directly teaching space mission resource trade-offs.

How to Run (Windows):

1. Download and extract the ZIP archive.

2. Run Beyond The Dust.exe (no installation required).

3. Follow the on-screen 60-second Flight Training tutorial instructions step by step to learn all mechanics before the real mission begins.
